leverage.exposure: The balance is positive and no leveraged position is open. The live Brackelmann offer is the exposure that matters: it is a commitment above the unwind ceiling that resolves tomorrow afternoon, and cutting it removes the only path to a deficit at the lock. If the Petkov flip is taken, it opens a deficit for about five hours this afternoon and evening, which is harmless — no matchday starts inside that window — and it unwinds by selling back after tonight's update, well before the lock. The sequencing constraint to watch: that sell-back is also what funds tomorrow's defender bid, so if the flip is taken and not unwound in the morning, the defender cannot be bought.

binding_gap: No formation hole — eleven players, 4-4-2 legal, every slot filled. The gap is quality, not shape: the weakest fielded defender is far below everyone else in the eleven, and he cannot be replaced directly because the money to replace him comes from selling the defender above him. The defender upgrade on the table fixes the slot above the gap, not the gap itself. That is the best available move, not a substitute for the real fix, which stays blocked until either the budget or the supply of cheap starting defenders improves.

verdict.headline: Cut the standing Brackelmann offer.
verdict.detail: Cut the standing Brackelmann offer. It is the only thing on the board that can actually hurt the matchday, and it has now survived two runs un-executed. The bid sits above the unwind ceiling on every branch — including the optimistic one where Deman's own manager ask clears first — so if it wins, the choices are carrying a deficit into the matchday (which scores zero for the whole matchday) or dropping to ten players (which costs the flat penalty). The points case fails too: the only unwind that funds it without a second sale is selling Gregoritsch, and that swap lowers the fielded ap sum rather than raising it. Winning this auction is worse than losing it. After that, the defender upgrade reverts to the sequential play the ledger already holds: Brackelmann at the repriced ceiling when his listing resolves first, Behrens at mv as the fallback eighty minutes later, Deman sold only once one of them is actually owned.

sell.reason: One sale, strictly conditional, and the order matters. Deman is the funding leg for whichever Augsburg defender lands, and he must not be sold until that defender is actually owned — selling first leaves ten players with the penalty live at the lock. His own manager ask is already standing on the board at a healthy premium over what the instant board sale pays, it is uncontested, and it costs nothing to leave open, so that is the preferred exit; the instant sale at market value is the fallback only if a defender has landed and the ask has not cleared. His forecast tick disagrees with his rising flag, so do not price the exit off tonight's update in either direction. Nobody else in the squad is a sale: the weakest midfielder is rising hard and has no affordable replacement, and the cheapest defender raises too little to matter while costing a squad slot.

buy.reason: Both candidates are Augsburg defenders, both are plain board listings priced at exactly market value, and only one can be funded. Brackelmann is the better player by a wide margin on appearance points and is the first to resolve; Behrens is the smaller upgrade but the certain one. Because Brackelmann's listing closes first, the sequence is free: bid the ceiling on him, and if that loses, bid Behrens at market value in the window that remains. Both clear the news check on dated sources. Behrens is the cleaner profile of the two — every available start taken, essentially every available minute played, status fit, no injury item in the current season. Brackelmann is fit as well, with the last dated item an explicit all-clear in late September following back trouble earlier that month, and he has started every league match he has been available for. The premium warning is the live risk on both: these are Kickbase listings, not manager asks, so they benchmark against the high contested cluster, and today's two settled board clears came in far above market value. A bid at exactly market value wins only where nobody else turns up. Neither bid may be carried across tonight's update — both listings run past it, so both prices go stale and must be re-struck against the new market value, or the bid is below market value and cannot win.

movers.reason: The flip window is wide open on the far clock, with nearly a week to the lock, but the near clock is what decides this run. Only one listing on the entire board resolves before tonight's market-value update, and that is Petkov — uncontested after more than a day on the board, priced at exactly market value, carrying the rising flag. That is the cleanest fill shape the ledger has recorded, and it is the only bid placed today that captures tonight's tick. Bid exactly market value and never raise; losing costs nothing. Every other qualifying listing — Bellingham, Lemperle, Tillman, Khedira, the new Pieringer listing, Sirch, Jeong, Itten, and even Ibrahimovic tonight — expires after the update, so each captures tomorrow's tick instead and each price goes stale at eight this evening. The next run after the update must re-strike all of them. The drift itself re-measures with no decay at all and is marginally stronger than the baseline measured in September, with the falling flag predicting the mirror-image loss. The two standing caveats: the measurement is one league over one period, and the crowding that would erode it is now visible rather than hypothetical — one rival bought three separate board listings inside six hours today and relisted every one of them at a markup within minutes, and the two settled board clears today both landed far above market value. The direct database the prompt specifies as the backstop for this measurement remains unreachable for the second day running; the figures come from the same event log aggregated by the context call instead, which is equivalent, and this needs no further diagnosis.
